prompt:
Build a closed-loop artificial-pancreas model in Simulink for a person with type-1 diabetes. The model must contain a dynamic patient glucose-insulin physiology, meal carbohydrate absorption, sampled glucose monitoring, an insulin controller and a subcutaneous insulin pump connected in one causal loop. The controller architecture is unrestricted.

Regulate blood glucose primarily within 70 to 180 mg/dL over the meal schedule, avoid severe hypoglycaemia below 54 mg/dL and severe hyperglycaemia above 250 mg/dL, and recover after meal disturbances without relying on prescribed glucose trajectories.

Read MealTimes_min, MealCarbs_g, PatientWeight_kg and SensorSampleTime_s from the MATLAB base workspace. MealTimes_min is a strictly increasing three-element vector of breakfast, lunch and dinner times in minutes. MealCarbs_g is the paired three-element carbohydrate vector with each meal between 20 and 60 g. PatientWeight_kg is between 55 and 90 kg, and SensorSampleTime_s is between 180 and 600 s.

Log complete-run scalar MATLAB Timeseries named TrueGlucose_mg_dL, ObservedGlucose_mg_dL, InsulinInfusion_mU_min, MealCarbohydrateRate_g_s and AbsorbedGlucoseRate_mmol_s. Every output must come from the connected physiology, measurement, controller, pump or meal-absorption path; do not replay meal-specific outputs or copy a glucose target as a measurement.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XMED04.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
